newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indonesia allocates 175-180,000 bpd June crude.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia allocates 175-180,000 bpd June crude.

text.p: Indonesia's state-owned Pertamina has allocated around 175-180,000 barrels per day (bpd) of export crude oil for June liftings, down from around 250,000 bpd in May, industry sources said on Friday.
They said the key Minas allocation was cut to 62,000 bpd in June from 73,000 bpd in May, while Duri was cut to 36,000 bpd from a month-earlier 60,000 bpd.
Pertamina did not allocate any Arun crude for export in June, compared with 24,000 bpd in May, the sources said.
The Cinta allocation was 4,000 bpd, down from 14,000 bpd, while 28,000 bpd of Widuri was allocated, up from 18,000 bpd.
Traders said the fall in the allocations was due to the need to feed a new 60,000 barrels-per-day crude unit at Balikpapan refinery.
Earlier on Friday, Samto Utomo, Pertamina's junior processing director, told Reuters in Jakarta the unit would be on stream late in June or early in July.
The unit is expected to test the use of Minas, Duri, Arun and possibly Widuri and Cinta, traders said.
